findings.title: Double-checked locking is missing the second check after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: GetWebAssets implements half of a double-checked locking pattern: it reads entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, then on miss acquires a write Lock and proceeds to read the manifest file unconditionally. After acquiring the write lock, the function never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache. As a result, in non-dev mode on a cold start, every concurrent caller that arrives while the cache is still nil will serialize on the mutex and each perform its own full file read (and any CDN read/write) and overwrite entryPointAssetsCache. The mutex prevents data corruption but does not prevent this thundering-herd I/O. The standard fix is to re-test entryPointAssetsCache under the write lock and return it early when populated (mirroring the original cfg.Env != Dev && ret != nil check).

findings.title: No regression test for the data race fix
findings.body: The PR's stated purpose is to fix a data race on entryPointAssetsCache, but no test is added. There is no new test invoking GetWebAssets concurrently (which would be required to actually catch the race with `go test -race`), nor any test verifying the lock semantics (e.g., that the cached pointer is observed atomically, or that concurrent cold-start calls do not corrupt the cache). Without a regression test, future refactors can silently reintroduce the race.

findings.title: Cached pointer is shared and not protected after return
findings.body: GetWebAssets returns the cached *dtos.EntryPointAssets pointer (entryPointAssetsCache) directly to callers. While the mutex now guards reads/writes of the cache slot itself and the initial SetContentDeliveryURL call, the returned pointer is shared with any other caller. Any caller that mutates the returned object (e.g., by calling SetContentDeliveryURL or otherwise) without holding entryPointAssetsCacheMu will race with other readers of the same object. The new locking protects the slot, not the pointee. The PR description claims the fix addresses the data race, but this residual race on the shared object is not addressed and is plausibly part of the original bug.

findings.title: Cache is overwritten with nil on transient read failure
findings.body: entryPointAssetsCache = result is executed unconditionally at the end of the write path, even when result is nil and err is non-nil (i.e., readWebAssetsFromFile failed). This clears the previously cached value and causes every subsequent non-dev caller to retry the file/manifest read on every request until a read succeeds, instead of continuing to serve a stale-but-valid cache during a transient failure. The assignment should be guarded by err == nil (and ideally result != nil) so a failed load does not wipe the existing cache.
